title: Rotor To Reef
style: world fusion electronic, 70 BPM builds to 92 BPM halftime groove, sub-bass as heartbeat, Spanish acoustic guitar thread weaving through industrial bass, Japanese koto pluck on verse breaks, West African djembe bridge, Indian Ocean underwater depth tones, didgeridoo drone undertone, male spoken word direct unhurried Southern hemisphere accent, no pitch correction breath between lines intentional, silence used as punctuation, sparse verses with instruments answering each line, full layered cultural voices on the chorus, half-time bridge with bass and one voice everything else gone, outro bass alone like a door closing slowly, not a hit a document, 336 hz subharmonic anchor under the bass
lyrics:
[Intro – rotor wash fading, Indian Ocean, sub-bass pulse alone]
WA coast.
Malaga yard.
Pete's my brother.
Helicopter to the reef.

[Verse 1 – sparse, each line breathes]
Steel roller door rising at first light
Brandon on the run sheet — numbers tight
Anna on the phone — bookings clean
Cameras watching everything unseen
I've been a deckie here and there
Salt in my eyes, rope in my hands
From Geraldton south to Abrolhos coral
Most people dream it.
They work the land.

[Pre-Chorus]
Two boats.
One partnership.
Indian Ocean doesn't care how you feel.

[Chorus – full, layered, every voice joins]
Rotor to reef — drop into blue
Paradise isn't a word, it's something you do
From Malaga steel to turquoise below
Abrolhos and Barrow — places few know
Helicopter shadow on ancient glass
Business trust that was built to last
WA coastline — 12,000 k's wide
We run that line — Pete's been my guide

[Verse 2 – percussive answers]
Fisheries changed the rules again
Demersal closed, bag limits tight
Compliance heavy — operators adapt
Or fold up their charts overnight
Pelicans gliding the wake line clean
Indian Ocean rolling between
Lobster grounds and coral shelf
Out here you earn it yourself

[Bridge – bass and one voice only, everything else gone silent]
Not everyone gets this view.
Most fly over WA and never look down.
They land in Perth.
They leave.
But Pete and Brandon stayed.
Built the boats with their hands.
Reef to yard.
Yard to reef.
That's the plan.

[Chorus – doubled]
Rotor to reef — drop into blue
Paradise isn't owned — it's earned by crew
Malaga yard to open sea
Western Australia — wild and free

[Outro – bass alone, door closing slowly]
Brother.
Boats.
WA.
